rows.title: TS-URGENet: A Three-stage Universal Robust and Generalizable Speech Enhancement Network
rows.semantic_reasoning: Packet loss is missing acoustic evidence that requires explicit reconstruction before ordinary enhancement.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Packet loss removes evidence rather than merely adding noise; a universal enhancer must reconstruct missing regions and then handle other distortions. Mechanism: The filling stage predicts lost regions, separation suppresses noise/reverb/clipping, and restoration repairs bandwidth, codec, and remaining loss. Result: The system ranked second in URGENT Track 1. Boundary: Challenge conditions, author-reported ranking, and no independent run limit the claim.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Fully End-to-end Streaming Open-vocabulary Keyword Spotting with W-CTC Forced Alignment
rows.semantic_reasoning: Open-vocabulary spotting integrates word alignment into end-to-end streaming recognition instead of relying on fixed keyword lists.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting must find arbitrary words without preparing word-aligned training data for every target. Mechanism: CTC paths supply word-span alignment while the text encoder and verifier are trained in the same pipeline. Result: The paper reports superior performance on the Libriphrase hard set. Boundary: Benchmark, language, and author-reported result limit generalization and independent reproducibility.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: A Silent Speech Decoding System from EEG and EMG with Heterogenous Electrode Configurations
rows.semantic_reasoning: Silent-speech decoding treats heterogeneous EEG/EMG sensing and patient transfer as central to assistive communication.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Silent-speech decoding could let speech-impaired users communicate without vocalizing, but biosignal recordings vary across people and electrode layouts. Mechanism: A shared model learns from varying EEG/EMG layouts while multitask objectives stabilize word classification across speakers and languages. Result: Accuracy is 95.3% for healthy participants and 54.5% for a patient, versus 70.1% and 13.2% for single-subject baselines. Boundary: Patient count, setup, calibration, and author-reported results limit clinical deployment claims.
